ideas.title: Start our one-shot workers with --safe-mode so they load nothing of the owner's own setup
ideas.problem: workers.run() builds `claude -p --output-format json --no-session-persistence --max-turns N --model M --system-prompt ... --tools ...` (workers.py line ~87). Claude's headless doc says a plain `claude -p` 'discovers and loads' hooks, skills, plugins, MCP servers, auto memory and CLAUDE.md like an interactive session. --tools limits built-in tools only, not MCP tools. So every Doulya/Sage/Vera/Serge/Calina/Israa/Omar/Tarek run can pick up whatever is in the owner's ~/.claude (skills list, claude.ai connectors, hooks, plugins). That is extra input tokens on each run against the plan allowance (SUBSCRIPTION_DAILY_VALUE_USD), extra start-up time, and a run that behaves differently if he installs something. --bare would fix this but needs an API key, so it is not an option for us.
ideas.proposal: 1) workers.py, in run(): add `--safe-mode` to `cmd` for the agents with an empty own folder (not for Ghassan, who passes cwd=... and may need the repo's context). 2) Fallback: if Claude Code answers with an unknown-option error (older bundled CLI than 2.1.169), run once without the flag and log `safe_mode_unsupported`; never send this to the paid API fallback. 3) Make it a team rule per the standing rule: rules.py key `workers.safe_mode` (on/off, default on) so Atlas can switch it off with `hq rule set` if some worker turns out to need a skill or MCP tool. Atlas (atlas_engine.py) stays as it is: he uses his own CLAUDE.md and skills on purpose. The change is in protected files (workers.py, rules.py is not): it is a Builder-chat job, not Ghassan's.
ideas.gain: Fewer input tokens per run and a faster start, and workers that behave the same whatever the owner installs on his PC. Size not known: Anthropic gives no number for the skill list; MCP tools are deferred, so only names and instructions count. Measure it: hq.db `usage` already stores input_tokens and cache_tokens per run; compare the average of the last 10 runs of one agent (say Vera) before and after.
ideas.test: 1) Normal: one Vera run with and without the flag on the same idea; pass = same structured_output keys, input_tokens + cache_tokens lower or equal, no error. 2) Edge: an old Claude CLI (or HQ_CLAUDE_PATH pointing at one) that rejects --safe-mode; pass = the run is retried without the flag once and `safe_mode_unsupported` is logged. 3) Failure case: with the rule off, the command line has no --safe-mode and runs exactly as today; also check Sage still gets WebSearch/WebFetch in safe mode (built-in tools should work; if not, drop the idea and say so).
ideas.confidence_why: Rests on Anthropic's own CLI reference and headless doc (A). Weakest link: nobody measured how much our workers load today, and the amount may be small if his setup is nearly empty; also the version of the CLI on his PC is unknown.
ideas.risks: A worker might rely on a user skill or MCP tool we forgot (tested by test 3, and the rule is a one-line off switch). Old CLI rejects the flag (handled by the retry). The flag was added in June 2026 and was undocumented for a few weeks (GitHub issue 66376), so check `claude --safe-mode --help` style behaviour on his PC once. No outside code, no licence issue.
